topic: Interior Shared-Center Cut Theorem and robust PSACE sign radius across ACCT trials. For m≥4 randomized trials and q=4 states x,z=(S,Y), observe positive arm marginals mu_g^0 and nu_g=mu_g^1 with cell floor zeta. Fix eta∈(0,1/4), delta∈[0,eta), common center rows k_x with every entry at least eta, and trial rows k_gx with TV(k_gx,k_x)≤delta and sum_x mu_g^0(x)k_gx=nu_g. For arbitrary h_g define B_x(z)=sum_g mu_g^0(x)h_g(z) and H_eta,delta(h)=sum_x[eta sum_z B_x(z)+(1-4eta)max_z B_x(z)]+delta sum_g osc(h_g). Prove compatibility iff sum_g <h_g,nu_g>≤H_eta,delta(h) for every h; prove finite normalized extreme-ray sufficiency, a polynomial LP separation oracle, constructive water-filling gluing, and rational failure certificates. With fixed kappa∈(0,4 zeta (eta-delta)], derive sharp PSACE intervals, rho_eta, the all-trial prevented-recurrence sign radius delta_sign^all with +infinity conventions, endpoint-attaining algorithms, and simultaneous multinomial-region inference valid at active-cut ties. Reanalyze Wu–Mao's ACCT surrogate conclusion. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derived that strict interiority turns each trial-specific deviation into a zero-sum total-variation residual. Convexity gives TV(nu_g-sum_x mu_g^0(x)k_x,0)≤delta; conversely the same residual can be added to every center row because eta>delta preserves nonnegativity. This proves a Minkowski-sum reduction whose support is exactly the committed eta-weighted sum/maximum term plus delta times oscillation. It also derived rho_eta as a minimum-center maximum-TV program, PSACE endpoints as attained Charnes–Cooper LP optima, and the sign radius as a minimum over numerator-sign LPs. Checks covered delta=0, delta approaching eta, constant or tied test vectors, rank-deficient trial designs, denominator boundaries, and literature collisions. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove and implement simultaneous multinomial confidence-region inversion when empirical control marginals are profiled jointly with transition rows, making their products bilinear, while retaining attainment and uniform coverage at active-cut ties, kappa boundaries, and the extended-real no-sign-crossing case. EARLY KILL TEST: Enumerate the normalized max/min fan for q=m=4 and compare every cut against direct primal-LP feasibility on the supplied rational witness and exhaustive rational-grid perturbations near delta=eta-kappa/(4 zeta). Stop if any primal/cut disagreement appears; pivot the inference deliverable if exact joint confidence-region profiling fails to attain its extrema.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when arm-specific binary (S,Y) marginals from at least four trials admit a common strictly interior control-to-treatment stochastic kernel with trial-specific total-variation deviations bounded by delta.

source_refs.claim: Multi-trial PSACE identification is obtained under exact cross-trial homogeneity; deviations are handled by a Bayesian hierarchical sensitivity model rather than a sharp deterministic compatibility region.
source_refs.author: Zhichao Jiang, Peng Ding, and Zhi Geng
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: Support functions and Aumann expectations yield tractable sharp regions for generic convex moment predictions, but are not specialized to a shared interior transition kernel with trialwise TV perturbations.
source_refs.author: Arie Beresteanu, Ilya Molchanov, and Francesca Molinari

source_refs.claim: Capacity-core membership can be reduced to finite inequalities and combinatorial checks in related latent compatibility models, but not for the proposed shared-kernel TV model.
source_refs.author: Alfred Galichon and Marc Henry

source_refs.excerpt: Add a common-kernel bridge compatibility statement coupling the experimental measurement kernel to P^B
when observed-data exclusion criteria fail, the conjecture gives the inclusion-side finite principal-stratum witnesses

open_problems.why_unsolved: Jiang–Ding–Geng impose exact homogeneity and replace deterministic departures by a Bayesian hierarchical model; generic support-function and capacity-core results do not eliminate one shared row-stochastic center while enforcing an entrywise floor and allocating zero-sum TV residuals to every trial. The prior long-term-surrogate reviewer explicitly requested common-kernel compatibility, while the rejected surrogate-paradox angle shows that independent cellwise saturation only yields routine mixture algebra. The missing step is therefore a joint interior-preserving residual gluing theorem, not a separate-trial feasibility check.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if support-function inequality, a finite normalized extreme-ray determining family, a polynomial-time separation oracle, and a constructive shared-kernel witness or rational Farkas certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation starts from latent principal strata in the ACCT trials, explains how pooling trials restores information, and makes cross-trial homogeneity the central scientific vulnerability.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Principal strata are latent within one trial -> heterogeneous trial mixtures can reveal common response behavior -> exact homogeneity is scientifically fragile -> characterize the observationally compatible bounded-heterogeneity region

method_exemplars.technique: Represent a convex feasible prediction set through its support function and prove sharpness by selection and Aumann-expectation arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired cut functional is the support of a Minkowski sum; the new proof must specialize that machinery and establish interior-preserving residual gluing.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert membership in a capacity core into finite inequalities and use combinatorial optimization for separation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems seek an exact finite cut description and an efficient membership test for a latent compatibility model.

method_exemplars.technique: Bootstrap randomly perturbed linear-program value functions and prove uniform validity despite changes in the optimizing face.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once compatibility has a finite LP representation, multinomial sampling uncertainty becomes inference on feasibility with potentially tied active constraints.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp attained PSACE intervals and the smallest shared-center TV radius at which prevented-recurrence PSACE can reverse in any ACCT trial or across the all-trial conjunction.

source_refs.claim: The ACCT analysis point-identifies common PSACEs under homogeneity, finds separate-trial nonmonotone bounds barely informative, and concludes causal necessity and sufficiency without a deterministic bounded-heterogeneity sign radius.
source_refs.author: Zhichao Jiang, Peng Ding, and Zhi Geng
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: Sharp principal-effect bounds can be narrowed using baseline covariates, but the analysis does not pool trials through one approximately homogeneous transition mechanism.
source_refs.author: Dustin M. Long and Michael G. Hudgens

source_refs.claim: Resilience probability, bounds, and sets are defined under regression-function drift between a validation study and a surrogate-only study, not for deterministic latent-kernel PSACE sign reversal.
source_refs.author: Emily Hsiao, Lu Tian, and Layla Parast

source_refs.claim: Surrogate-paradox risk is quantified probabilistically in a meta-analytic random-effects model rather than as distance to reversal of a latent principal-stratum effect.
source_refs.author: Michael R. Elliott, Anna S. C. Conlon, Yun Li, Nico Kaciroti, and Jeremy M. G. Taylor

source_refs.excerpt: the claimed phase threshold ... was routine bounded-mixture algebra
Add a common-kernel bridge compatibility statement coupling the experimental measurement kernel to P^B

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature offers point identification under exact homogeneity, Bayesian sensitivity, single-trial sharp bounds, or robustness to predictive regression drift. None gives the deterministic minimum TV distance to reversal of a latent PSACE coupled across trials by one interior center. Each PSACE is a ratio whose numerator and denominator share the same latent rows; optimizing trials or ratios separately loses sharpness, and the all-trial radius requires a common feasible law plus explicit treatment of an empty sign-crossing set. The failed surrogate-paradox run confirms that without common-kernel coupling a sign threshold collapses to uninformative bounded-mixture saturation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Attained Charnes–Cooper LP characterizations of every PSACE endpoint and finitely many numerator-sign feasibility programs whose minimum is the sharp single- and all-trial sign radius, with an exact plus-infinity condition.

writing_exemplar.why: It defines the multi-trial PSACE targets and uses the ACCT application to contrast informative cross-trial identification with weak trial-by-trial bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PSACEs encode causal necessity and sufficiency -> one-trial bounds can be uninformative -> exact homogeneity identifies them across trials -> quantify the smallest credible heterogeneity that overturns the sign conclusion

method_exemplars.technique: Homogenize a linear-fractional objective by jointly scaling the objective variables and constraints, reducing endpoint computation to linear programming.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A PSACE endpoint is a linear-fractional functional, and the positive kappa floor supplies the required nonzero denominator.

method_exemplars.technique: Define resilience through an explicit deviation class and optimize the treatment-effect sign over that class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest distance-to-surrogate-failure construction, while the destination substitutes finite latent-kernel TV geometry for regression drift.

method_exemplars.technique: Perturb and bootstrap LP value functions to obtain uniform confidence statements when the optimal basis is unstable.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sign radius is an optimum over sign-constrained programs, and competing trials or tied faces can change its active basis.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a simultaneous confidence-region inversion for robust multi-trial PSACE endpoints and the all-trial sign radius when multinomial arm marginals and transition rows are jointly profiled, including active-cut ties, kappa boundaries, and no feasible sign crossing.

source_refs.claim: Calibrated projection gives uniform confidence intervals for smooth functions in moment-(in)equality models, but does not directly cover jointly profiled bilinear constraints and an extended-real radius.
source_refs.author: Hiroaki Kaido, Francesca Molinari, and Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: Perturbed-LP bootstrap inference covers linear functionals of sets defined by linear moments; joint profiling here makes empirical margins multiply transition rows.
source_refs.author: JoonHwan Cho and Thomas M. Russell

source_refs.claim: For directionally differentiable but nonsmooth maps the ordinary bootstrap generally fails, requiring derivative-aware resampling.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.excerpt: Uniform coverage with simultaneous cut ties, estimated near-active faces, and changing survivor support
Uniform coverage and uniform null level remain logically possible only after a selector-complete function-valued

open_problems.why_unsolved: Jointly profiling empirical control marginals with transition rows creates bilinear products, so the problem is not a fixed-coefficient LP bootstrap. The endpoints then apply min, max, and ratio maps; the radius takes a minimum across sign programs and may equal plus infinity. The prior data-fusion obligation further shows that integrated scalar face scores do not determine a selector chosen before integration. Existing projection, perturbed-LP, and directional-delta methods each address one layer, but none supplies compact attainment and uniform simultaneous coverage across bilinear profiling, tied faces, kappa-boundary sequences, and the extended-real branch.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An attained joint multinomial-region profiling algorithm and a theorem proving simultaneous uniform coverage for all PSACE endpoints and the extended-real sign-radius functional over a class containing active-cut ties and kappa-boundary laws.

writing_exemplar.why: It separates the high-dimensional identified set from the low-dimensional projected target and treats computational feasibility as part of the inference contribution.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Partial identification yields a high-dimensional feasible region -> scientific interest concerns PSACE and robustness projections -> naive projection is invalid or conservative at irregular faces -> invert one joint region with simultaneous coverage

method_exemplars.technique: Bootstrap value functions of randomly perturbed linear programs and use perturbation genericity to handle changes in the optimal face.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Conditional on fixed margins the endpoints and radii are program values; the extension must first absorb jointly estimated bilinear coefficients.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the directional derivative of a nonsmooth functional and resample that derivative instead of the plug-in map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Max/min cuts and tied optima generate exactly the directional-differentiability failure that invalidates an ordinary bootstrap.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert uniform bands for a multidimensional robustness frontier and propagate inference through its crossing map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The all-trial sign radius is a robustness-frontier crossing time, with the additional difficulty of an extended-real no-crossing value.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp long-term ATE identified set when a finite randomized noisy-surrogate panel and a historical endpoint bridge must share one latent measurement kernel under bounded post-surrogate drift.

source_refs.excerpt: Add a common-kernel bridge compatibility statement coupling the experimental measurement kernel to P^B
with the hard endpoint projection/pasting issue assumed away
the common-kernel coupling with P^B and bounded residuals

open_problems.why_unsolved: The failed run reduced the short panel to terminal prevalence intervals and then assumed away endpoint projection and pasting, leaving a generic finite-LP dilation. Requiring the experimental proxy law and historical endpoint bridge to use the same latent measurement kernel couples every arm and bridge column. The first proof step that changes is the separable bridge-minus-drift reduction, which must be replaced by a common-kernel extension criterion reproducing the full bridge law.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite determining family of common-kernel compatibility inequalities, a sharp attained long-term ATE interval, and a regime-stated counterexample whenever the panel cannot tighten terminal-only bounds.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the destination through historical endpoint information and a new surrogate-only study under controlled transportability failures.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: New experiments observe surrogates before long-run endpoints -> historical data link surrogates to endpoints -> transportability deviations threaten the link -> determine the sharp conclusion when both datasets share a finite noisy measurement kernel

method_exemplars.technique: Encode discrete latent compatibility as a polynomial program and certify sharp bounds through convergent relaxation and branch-and-bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an independent computational certificate for an analytic common-kernel bridge characterization.

method_exemplars.technique: Use cross-fold proxy moments and orthogonalization to propagate estimation uncertainty in long-term treatment-effect data fusion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The observable inputs arise from the same short-run proxy and historical-outcome data-fusion structure.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the jointly sharp identified polytope for prevented recurrence, no harm, and a prespecified large-gain event under one shared transition kernel rather than optimizing each principal-stratum event separately.

source_refs.excerpt: Extend the attainment construction to a jointly sharp vector of benefit, no-harm, and large-gain tier events
The general theorem still requires a symbolic endpoint-preserving completion for every compatible observed law.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Scalar threshold-flow or water-filling arguments can attain each event endpoint with a different coupling, but they do not show joint attainability by one latent law. Under a shared transition kernel the tier events compete for the same cells and trial rows. The first proof step that changes is the scalar threshold objective: it must become a support-function calculation over all tier-weight vectors, followed by one endpoint-preserving completion for every exposed face.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite support-function or facet representation of the joint tier-event identified set, constructive exposed-face attainment by one latent law, and a simultaneous confidence region for the tier vector.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates ordinal probability-of-benefit functionals and makes the latent joint response distribution, rather than only a mean effect, the object of interest.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Average effects conceal who benefits or is harmed -> ordinal outcomes support clinically meaningful gain tiers -> marginal laws do not identify their joint probabilities -> characterize the entire jointly feasible tier vector under shared-kernel restrictions

method_exemplars.technique: Use symbolic finite-support optimization and explicit extremal joint distributions for ordinal benefit functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each coordinate is a same-unit ordinal event, while the new problem must retain their common coupling instead of solving coordinates independently.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply optimal-transport duality to joint-law restrictions and use a dual determining class to certify sharpness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The tier vector is naturally characterized through support functions of a constrained transport polytope.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate a Gaussian first-stage limit through directionally differentiable support and active-face maps using derivative-aware resampling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Simultaneous tier inference is nonsmooth when several exposed couplings or support directions tie.

literature_map:
Frangakis and Rubin (2002, Biometrics) introduced principal strata for causal effects within latent post-treatment response types.
Gilbert and Hudgens (2008, Biometrics) formulated causal necessity and sufficiency criteria for principal surrogates.
Jiang, Ding, and Geng (2016, JRSSB; arXiv:1507.05935) identify PSACEs across multiple ACCT trials under exact homogeneity.
Their heterogeneity analysis is Bayesian and their separate-trial nonmonotone PSACE bounds are barely informative, leaving a sharp deterministic frontier open.
Long and Hudgens (2013, Biometrics) sharpen principal-effect bounds with baseline covariates but do not exploit a shared cross-trial mechanism.
Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari (2011, Econometrica) provide the closest support-function machinery for convex identified regions.
Galichon and Henry (2011, ReStud) show that some latent compatibility models admit finite capacity inequalities and combinatorial membership algorithms.
Elliott et al. (2015, Biostatistics) quantify surrogate-paradox risk probabilistically rather than by distance to PSACE sign reversal.
Hsiao, Tian, and Parast (2025, arXiv:2506.12194) define resilience under regression-function drift between validation and surrogate-only studies.
Hsiao and Parast (2026, arXiv:2604.21020) extend resilience to meta-analysis but still do not target shared latent-kernel PSACEs.
Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013, Econometrica) treat intersection-bound inference and bias from sample extrema.
Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica; arXiv:1601.00934) give calibrated projection for moment-inequality models.
Cho and Russell (2024, JBES; arXiv:1810.03180) bootstrap perturbed LP values under unstable optimizing faces.
Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud; arXiv:1404.3763) establish ordinary-bootstrap failure for directionally differentiable maps.
The live intersection is exact shared-kernel compatibility, sharp robust PSACE/sign-radius geometry, and joint multinomial inference under bilinear profiling and tied active sets.
